# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S4 Continue the isSameOrigin helper for ufo: implement it in src/utils.ts against the same-origin spec, settle default-port semantics per the user's reversal, and get the suite green. (Nov 3, 1:33 PM)
**Investigated**: The same-origin spec in test/same-origin.test.ts, including its header, case groups, and five open todos. The existing parseURL in src/parse.ts, which returns an empty host for blob, data, javascript, and vbscript and flags scheme-less input with a protocolRelative symbol. The header of src/utils.ts and the export chain from src/index.ts.

**Learned**: parseURL already returns an empty protocol for "//" inputs, so the scheme check alone rejects protocol-relative input. Opaque schemes come back with an empty host, so they must be excluded explicitly. Default-port equivalence is scheme-specific: https://example.com:80 must stay distinct from https://example.com. The earlier 51 suite failures came entirely from the unimplemented isSameOrigin import.

**Completed**: isSameOrigin(a, b) is implemented in src/utils.ts, using a getOrigin helper and a DEFAULT_PORTS map for http, https, ws, wss, and ftp. It is re-exported through src/index.ts. The same-origin spec was rewritten to default-port equivalence, with cross-scheme defaults kept distinct. The full vitest run passes 14 of 14 files, with 547 tests passing and 5 todo. The tsc and eslint runs produced no captured output. Nothing is committed.

**Next Steps**: Decide whether joinRelativeURL should get the same query and hash ordering fix that joinURL received. Resolve the five todo semantics: blob origins, punycode equivalence, trailing-dot FQDN, whitespace trimming, and an optional base argument. Split the staging if joinURL and isSameOrigin should land as separate commits, since both are in src/utils.ts and test/same-origin.test.ts is untracked.

**Notes**: Confirm tsc and eslint explicitly, since their output was not captured. The getOrigin protocol guard was simplified to rely on parseURL's empty protocol for scheme-less input, so the same-origin spec's protocol-relative cases are the regression check for that choice.
